title: catalog fold hashes raw JSON bytes (comments + formatting), so cosmetic edits to data/*.json silently invalidate every golden
evidence: core/catalog.odin: "// FNV-1a-64 over the sim-relevant catalog bytes in fixed order (hash.odin)." / "catalogs_hash_sources :: proc(src: ^Catalog_Sources) -> u64 {" / "fold(&h, src.node_types)" ... "fold(&h, src.balance)" ; harness/catalogs.odin: "nt, e1 := os.read_entire_file_from_path("data/node_types.json", context.temp_allocator)" ; data/node_types.json: "{ "_comment": "Node-type catalog (GDD § M3, ODN-5)..." ; harness/run.odin: "if header.catalog_hash != cat.hash { ... replay: catalog drift — log %016x vs current %016x (defined rejection, ODN-11)"
detail: The fold consumes the entire raw file bytes (verified: byte-exact FNV-1a-64 over the raw six files reproduces 250679b1940fb87b; the files carry large _comment fields). A comment-only/reformat edit to any data/*.json therefore breaks the replay gate and forces the wholesale 35-manifest + 33-log re-bless this chunk represents — the 'sim-relevant' comment overstates the fold's precision.
recommended_fix: Correct the catalogs_hash_sources doc comment to state raw-byte semantics (comments/whitespace folded), so future agents don't treat comment edits as replay-safe; keep the conservative raw-byte design.
